summary: Dry Out, Rev Out and ER Out become Neo Verb's Mix, Late and Early, with the output connections making up the level the crossfade takes; Rev Time, Pre-Delay and High Cutoff carry over in seconds and Hz.

rules.why: Jeskola Reverb sets dry and wet levels apart; Neo Verb crossfades. The wet gains are the level difference between the two machines' tails (+8.7 dB) and early reflections (+9.6 dB) at the same settings, measured on Windows (ReBuzzTests/AgentReplaceTests.cs).
Rev Time reads in seconds; the profile's tail (0.7 s to −60 dB at 1.0 s with the wet 14.5 dB down) fits a T60, which is what Neo Verb's Decay is.
the tail's high cut; Neo Verb's damping corner goes from 1 kHz up.

remarks: Jeskola Reverb is mono (ReBuzz gives a mono native effect left + right summed: the input connections take +6 dB to match); Neo Verb is stereo. Width differs by design; set Width to 0% for a mono tail.
The algorithms differ (a 2000s Buzz reverb against a 16-line feedback delay network): the tail's colour and density are not the same, its level and length are.
evidence: Machines/Manifests/Effects/Jeskola Reverb.machine.json (curated: levels 20·log10(raw/4096) dB, Rev Time 0.1–6.4 s, Pre-Delay 0–100 ms, High Cutoff 100–16384 Hz)
Machines/Manifests/machine-profile.json: Jeskola Reverb's gain +6.2 dB at the defaults, output correlation 1.0, tail 0.7 s
Machines/NeoVerb/Engine/VerbEngine.cs: out = in + (wet − in)·Mix, wet = Early·ER·0.5 + Late·tail
